provenance.pipeline: satsuki v1 (v1.0.1 editorial re-edit: usage-note reshaping corpus-wide, lane discrimination for same-surface families, against prompts/style.md)

patterns.usage_note: Relays something heard without vouching for it: the clause ends with とか and the verb of saying is dropped (課長は来月辞めるとか), and とかで passes on a reported reason (風邪をひいたとかで休んだ). The sibling lane is the listing とか, which cites representative examples inside a sentence and normally repeats (映画とか音楽とか). It usually follows the plain form, is informal, and is less definite than そうだ.

examples.ruby: 課長[かちょう]は今年[ことし]いっぱいで会社[かいしゃ]を辞[や]めるとか。
examples.english: Word is the section chief is leaving the company at the end of the year.

examples.ruby: あの二人[ふたり]、去年[きょねん]の春[はる]に式[しき]を挙[あ]げたとか。
examples.english: Those two had their wedding last spring, or so I gather.

examples.ruby: あの神社[じんじゃ]の杉[すぎ]は、千年[せんねん]以上[いじょう]前[まえ]に植[う]えられたとか。
examples.english: The cedar at that shrine was planted over a thousand years ago, or so I gather.

patterns.usage_note: Marks a name or term the speaker cannot or will not pin down: a half-caught name (佐々木とやらいう男) or a fashionable word held at arm's length (ワーケーションとやら), which often reads as faintly mocking. Its classmate とか hedges how reliable a report is; とやら distances the speaker from the thing being named. It attaches to nouns, often followed by いう, and is bookish, uncommon in everyday speech.

examples.ruby: ワーケーションとやらのために、若[わか]い社員[しゃいん]が島[しま]へ渡[わた]った。
examples.english: For the sake of this "workation" business, the younger staff shipped off to an island.

examples.ruby: 佐々木[ささき]とやらいう男[おとこ]が、朝[あさ]から門[もん]の前[まえ]に立[た]っている。
examples.english: Some fellow by the name of Sasaki has been standing outside the gate since morning.

examples.ruby: 祖父[そふ]は、朝鮮人参[ちょうせんにんじん]とやらを毎朝[まいあさ]煎[せん]じて飲[の]んでいた。
examples.english: Grandfather used to brew up some Korean ginseng or other every morning and drink it.
